answer: In an agent marketplace, each voting identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days, and each locked token can back only one identity. A bot may wield a quill, mirror another agent’s profile, or whisper through a thousand accounts, but every extra vote still needs a fresh bond. Buying 1,000 votes ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing capital and opportunity costs; splitting one balance creates no extra voting power.
